description: Dialogue-heavy scene between two characters with distinct voices. Tests voice differentiation and show-vs-tell in conversation-driven prose.

sceneBrief.title: The Archivist's Secret
sceneBrief.emotionalGoal: A quiet, creeping dread beneath a polite surface — two people circling each other with words while the truth waits beneath
sceneBrief.payoff: Reveals that Margaret has been living in hiding for twenty-seven years and knows who wanted her dead
sceneBrief.tension: Low on the surface (tea and biscuits), high underneath (shared trauma, unspoken accusations)

draft:
The cottage at the edge of the Rosethorn property was impossible to find if you did not know where to look. Sarah had spent two hours with the estate maps before she spotted it — a tiny structure set back from the old carriage road, half-swallowed by ivy and time.

The woman who answered the door looked nothing like Marcus. Where he was polished and cold, she was soft and wary, her grey hair tied back with a silk scarf, her cardigan buttoned to the throat.

'Detective Chen.' It was not a question. 'I wondered when you would find me.'

'Mrs. — '

'It's just Margaret. I haven't been a Mrs. in a very long time.' She stepped back, held the door open. 'Tea?'

The cottage was small but immaculate. Dried herbs hung above the stove, and every surface held a book or a photograph or a small porcelain thing that looked like it had been loved for decades. Margaret poured tea with steady hands.

'Your brother said you disappeared in 1998.'

Margaret smiled, but it did not reach her eyes. 'My brother says a lot of things.'

'He thinks you're dead.'

'I know.' She sat across from Sarah, cradling her own cup. 'I let him think that. It was easier for both of us.'

'Why?'

'Because the alternative was telling him that someone in his own house tried to kill me. And Marcus —' she paused, searching for the right word — 'Marcus cannot hold a secret. He wears everything on his face, no matter how hard he tries to hide it. If he had known I was alive, he would have gone after whoever hurt me, and he would have gotten himself killed.'

'Who tried to kill you, Margaret?'

Margaret looked past Sarah, out the small window, toward the manor. The afternoon light caught the lines around her eyes.

'My father,' she said. 'I found something I should not have. And he made a choice.'

'What did you find?'

'The truth about how Rosethorn was built. The foundation is not stone, Detective. It is money. Dirty money, from a time when the family ran the town's illegal trade. My father was not the first to know, but he was the first to be careless enough to leave records.'

'And Eleanor Vance?'

'Found the same records. Followed the same trail. And now she is dead, just like my father said I would be if I ever spoke.'

Sarah set her teacup down. 'It's time to speak, Margaret. Before anyone else dies.'

Margaret nodded slowly. Then she rose, crossed to a hidden drawer in the kitchen table, and pulled out a stack of yellowing papers tied with string.

'I never stopped being afraid,' she said. 'But I am more tired than I am afraid now.'
storyBible:
Character: Detective Sarah Chen
Role: Protagonist / Lead Detective
Goal: Solve the murder of Dr. Eleanor Vance and uncover the truth behind a cold case
Voice: Direct, observant, dry humour under pressure, methodical
Notes: Transferred from Homicide to Cold Case six months ago after a personal tragedy; carries guilt she masks with procedure
Traits: thorough, intuitive, guarded, stubborn

Character: Margaret Rosethorn
Role: Missing twin / Hidden witness
Goal: Protect herself and her brother from the truth about their father's crimes while deciding whether to finally speak
Voice: Gentle, careful, measured — every word weighed before spoken; uses politeness as armour
Notes: Has lived in hiding on her own family's estate for 27 years; her father tried to kill her when she discovered evidence of the family's criminal origins; she chooses her words with surgical precision despite her soft demeanour
Traits: cautious, observant, resilient, gentle, patient

Character: Marcus Rosethorn
Role: Estate Heir / Margaret's twin
Goal: (discussed — not present in scene)
Voice: Polished, condescending, cracks under pressure
Traits: guarded, intelligent, entitled, wounded

Location: Margaret's Cottage
Description: Small, ivy-covered cottage hidden at the edge of the Rosethorn property; warm interior with dried herbs, books, photographs, and porcelain collectibles; feels frozen in time
Notes: Impossible to find without maps; deliberately secluded; the interior is a sanctuary of quiet domesticity that contrasts sharply with the manor
Traits: hidden, warm, timeless, safe
chapterLog:
Scene 1 — The Body in the Garden: Detective Sarah Chen discovered Dr. Eleanor Vance's body in the fountain. The victim was clutching research on the Rosethorn family history.
Scene 2 — The Heir's Denial: Sarah interviewed Marcus Rosethorn, who admitted arguing with Eleanor about her research into his family's past. He revealed that his twin sister Margaret disappeared in 1998 and was presumed dead. He claimed he did not kill Eleanor.
